Journal.VoteNul: The vote is closed: no one is chosen.
Journal.VoteChapelle: The village chooses who will sleep in the Chapel.

RevelerALaMort.Aide: A dead villager's role is shown to everyone.

MortsVoientTout.Aide: A dead player sees everyone's role on the game table (and no longer votes).

DureeVote.Aide: Timer shown in the banner and on the game table; at zero, the vote closes by itself (the execution still needs confirming). 0 = no timer: the GM closes the vote.

ChanceEpier.Aide: Probability (0 to 1) that the Child of the Mist, when she spies on the pack, is caught and devoured instead of the prey (0.5 by default).

AnnoncesEnChat.Aide: Deaths and victory are also announced in the chat.

CanalDesMorts.Aide: The dead may talk among themselves: the active GM relays their messages to the dead and the GMs only (no chat message, which Foundry would deliver to everyone). Otherwise, they can only write to the GM.

SalonsAutomatiques.Aide: With Foundry built-in voice (A/V): at night only the wolves talk to each other; the dead speak only to the dead; a silenced player stays quiet during the debate and the vote. Each browser mutes what it must not hear, and its own microphone when it must stay quiet. The GM always hears everything. Unchecked: everyone talks to everyone.

RepartirAZero.Nom: Start fresh every time the world is launched
RepartirAZero.Aide: A werewolf game is never resumed: when the world is launched, the game in progress is erased (roles, trades, deaths, chat, secrets), the AI players leave the village and everyone gets the base token back; the village returns to setup, the players' villagers ready for the deal. The Chronicles and the hall of fame remain. Reloading the page (F5) resets nothing.
RepartirAZero.Fait: New vigil: the village starts fresh.

PlateauInteractif.Aide: Night choices, votes and day powers are made by clicking tokens, from the banner. Unchecked: the choice and vote windows open as before.

SignalTour.Nom: Signal when it is my turn
SignalTour.Aide: A soft chime, for me only, when a night choice or a vote is waiting for me; if I am looking at another tab, its title blinks until I come back.

Bailli.Aide: On the first day, the village elects a Bailiff: their vote counts double in the execution vote, they break ties and, upon death, name their successor. Applies from the next deal.

Masques.Aide: When roles are dealt, the pack secretly receives two or three Village roles that are not in play, which it can safely claim. Never in a black plague game.

DernierSouffle.Aide: Each dead villager keeps one vote, once, for an execution vote. Applies from the next deal.

Almanach.Aide: At each dawn, a drawn omen changes the rule of the day or of the next night, announced to all. Applies from the next deal.

GensDePassage.Aide: A player arriving mid-game joins as a traveller (public role, secret side); a player can leave the vigil without dying; the village can vote to exile a traveller.

Banc.Aide: Everyone accuses once a day; the accused are judged one by one (for or against); half of the living votes are needed to execute. Applies from the next deal.

GlasDuDeuil.Aide: Each innocent executed by vote tolls the bell and gives the pack a growing collective power (a vision, a faceless vote, the shroud). Applies from the next deal.

PetiteTablee.Aide: The mode for 1 to 4 humans completed by 2 to 8 AI players (4 to 12 seats): a short pack (from two wolves on: a white first night, and the pack must outnumber the others to win), humans never all wolves nor all in the same camp, a deal that favours (without guarantee) a lantern with a human and the shadow on both sides of the table, ties settled by lot, the final bell set automatically. Remembers the last level chosen at the Game Table; when checked, « Replay » and the AI GM compose a small table.

VeilleeDeFete.Aide: The holiday vigil of a game dealt without an explicit choice (by the AI GM, or « Replay »): none by default, the one the calendar suggests that day, or a named vigil. The Game Table suggests the calendar's one; the narrator decides. Applied at the next deal.
VeilleeDeFete.Aucune: None by default (the previous game keeps its own)
VeilleeDeFete.Date: By the calendar (today's holiday, if any)

EffetsVisuels.Aide: Night mist, glow of dawn and of victory, a slight screen shake at each death. Nothing moves if your system asks for reduced motion.

InnocentSuitAieul.Aide: If the Greybeard falls at the village's hand (vote, poison, Poacher), a Village Innocent already pardoned dies with him: the village loses its wisdom. Taken at the deal.

LeVillage.Aide: Personalities (Prior, Alehouse Keeper, Tenant Farmers…) hold the village buildings: a public power on top of their secret role; the other players are Drifters. Kept from one game to the next (the “The Village” box of the Game Table changes it).

Chandelles.Aide: A candle before each player, on their card of the Game Table: blown out at their death (the pack's victim in the morning, the condemned after the vote). Kept from one game to the next (the “Variants” boxes of the Game Table change it).

ChandellesAngoissantes.Aide: With the candles: each wolf blows out a candle himself at night; if they did not all blow out the same one, the pack has no victim, and the village sees the dark candles in the morning.

ChaineDesInnocents.Aide: The day's condemned is not voted: standing, each in turn seats a villager whose innocence they vouch for, starting from the left neighbour of the last eliminated; the last one standing is condemned. No Dock with it.

MurDesMurmures.Aide: Each night, every living player may write a short anonymous sentence; in the morning the wall is read to all, sentences mixed. The authors are never known, not even to the narrator.

DoubleVisage.Aide: Small twist: a visible role for each, and a secret allegiance card that sets their side. Big twist: two secret cards per player. 7 to 18 players; neither at the small table nor with the black plague.

AllegeanceLoupEnPlus.Nom: Two Faces: one more wolf allegiance
AllegeanceLoupEnPlus.Aide: With Two Faces only: one more wolf allegiance card in the deck, in place of a villager allegiance (small and big twist). The book's deck favours the village at large tables: advised from 16 players with the small twist (and at 13), from 12 with the big one; below that, the book's deck.

Vendanges.Aide: One more wolf, and every power tipsy until the end of the vigil (see the variant rules). Neither at the small table nor with the black plague.

Envoutement.Aide: The pack's victims do not die: they lose their powers and stay enthralled, in secret. An enthralled victim condemned drags the earlier ones along; the pack wins once it has enthralled the second-to-last villager. Neither at the small table nor with the black plague.

BatimentsDuVillage.Aide: None (a simple game, with the characters only), drawn at random by the setup (as before), or chosen by the GM at the Game Table. The Table keeps the last choice.

MetiersEnJeu.Aide: Each player receives a public trade on top of their role. Unticked: a game without trades. At the “The Pact” level, never any trade.

Gazette.Aide: The Event cards: every morning but the first, the last player eliminated reads one out, which changes the rule. Without the Almanac of mists. Applies from the next deal.

GazetteRythme.Aide: A card every morning, every other morning, or one morning in three.

GazetteChoix.Nom: The Gazette: the narrator picks the cards
GazetteChoix.Aide: No draw: the narrator has whichever card they want read out, whenever they want (Game Table).

CrieurPublic.Aide: The Bailiff names a Town Crier, whom the narrator entrusts with Gazette cards; every morning, they may read one out. With or without the Gazette.

CartesDuCrieur.Nom: The Town Crier: number of cards
CartesDuCrieur.Aide: Drawn at random before the game (the book advises five at most).

PartageIllumine.Nom: The Zealot: how the village is split
PartageIllumine.Aide: The criterion that splits the village into two groups, announced at the start: the bank, or a visible trait of the characters.

Erreurs.PasMJ: Only the active GM can run the game (lakour-loups).
Erreurs.PasDeJoueurs: No player to deal roles to.
Erreurs.SansRole: Both villagers must have a role.
Erreurs.PasDeVillageois: You do not play any villager.
Erreurs.PasDeMJ: No GM is connected: the power cannot be applied.
Erreurs.RolesInconnus: Unknown roles, or missing from the content: {roles}.
Erreurs.PersonneAReveiller: No one to wake for "{role}" tonight.
Erreurs.SansCoffre: The AI GM module (lakour-mj-ia) must be active: its vault keeps the game's secrets (roles, sides, night choices). Enable it, then deal.
Erreurs.SansCleCoffre: AI GM vault closed in this browser: its key stayed in the browser where the world was prepared. The game goes on, but its secrets stay only in this browser until the key returns: do not switch browsers mid-game. To bring it back, import the backup key (Settings › MJ IA › Vault) or connect another GM who has it: at the Vigils, the players keep no share of it.
Erreurs.FicheVerrouillee: Only the GM may change the villagers of the game.
Erreurs.NotesSecretes: A villager's notes reach every player's browser: a secret block is not kept there. Put it in a GM-only journal.
Erreurs.SecretsAbsents: This browser does not (yet) hold the up-to-date secrets of the current game: nothing is written. The vault is reopened as soon as the key is back (backup key imported, or another connected GM who has it).
Erreurs.MJInactif: Only the active GM holds the game's secrets: role, side, lover and "Revealed" are set from that GM's browser.
Erreurs.Votants: Choose at least one living villager who may vote; there must be a Whipping Boy who died of a tie.

Carnet.Nouveau: A secret message awaits you in your notebook.
Carnet.Aide: What the narrator tells you, and you alone. Never copy it to the common channel.

Bandeau.NouvellePartie: New game! Open "My role" to discover yours.

Aide.bandeauValider: Send your choice to the narrator: the players selected by clicking their token.
Aide.bandeauPasser: Do nothing this time: your turn passes, with no target.
Aide.bandeauListe: Open the list of allowed players, if you prefer choosing without the map.

Aide.bandeauAnnuler: Give up this power for now: nothing is used.
Aide.bandeauVoter: Open the list of the accused to vote (you can also click a token). You may change your mind while the vote is open.
Aide.bandeauOuvrirVote: Start the village vote: every living player names who they accuse, within the time set in the settings; at zero, it closes by itself.
Aide.bandeauCloreVote: Stop the vote without waiting for the timer and count the votes; executing the chosen is asked next.
Aide.bandeauPeste: Cry "It's the black plague!" to the village. If true, the game ends and the village wins; if false, you are hanged for spreading panic.
Aide.bandeauVoteBailli: Starts the Bailiff election, before the execution vote: each living villager names a candidate; the winner gets a double vote and breaks ties.

Salon.taniere: 🐺 Den: you speak to the wolves
Salon.Aide: Voice room: what Foundry built-in voice lets you say and hear right now.

Bandeau.MonRoleAide: Your secret notebook: your role card and what you learn at night (only you can see it).

Attente.nuit: Night falls on Brumecombe: everyone stays home.
Attente.jour: The village debates on the square.

Bandeau.VoteBailli: Bailiff election: click your candidate's token.

Parole.Mort: You are dead: the living no longer hear you. You may write to the narrator (whisper to the GM: only the GM receives it).
Parole.Silence: You are silenced: you cannot speak during today's debate and vote (a word whispered to the GM reaches the GM alone).
Parole.CanalDesMorts: You are dead: your messages now reach only the other dead and the narrator (relayed by the GM, never through Foundry's chat).
Parole.Chuchotement: During a game, no whispering between players: Foundry would deliver it to every browser. Speak aloud, or write to the GM only.
Parole.JetAveugle: 🎲 Blind roll sent to the GM.

NouvellePartie.Annonce: New game! The roles of the {n} villagers are dealt in secret.

Detail.juge: The Justice of the Peace ({nom}) may still cancel this vote.
Detail.emporter: {nom} chooses whom to take along (or no one).
Detail.sansSecrets: This browser does not hold the night's secrets.
Detail.bancVide: (Nobody is accused: wait for accusations during the debate, or let night fall.)
Detail.emporterDemande: {nom} is choosing whom to take along right now; you may decide in their stead.
Detail.chaine: Chain of Innocents: {nom} names an innocent; closing waits for the last one standing.
Detail.inondation: (The Flood: no vote today; let night fall.)

Etapes.departage: Waiting: the Bailiff ({nom}) breaks the tie…
Etapes.succession: Waiting: {nom}, the late Bailiff, hands over the seal…

Preparation.IAAbsente: Enable the AI GM module to add AI players.
Preparation.IAIndisponible: AI players require the AI GM module.
Preparation.Trop: More roles than seats: remove some.

Voix.Desactivee: Foundry voice chat is disabled in this world: nobody can hear each other.
Voix.ActiverAide: Switch the world to "Audio only" (no video at the Vigils). Voice rooms then follow the game. Each player picks a microphone in Configure Audio/Video › Client.
Voix.Activee: Audio enabled: everyone can pick a microphone in Configure Audio/Video.
Voix.MicroAide: Grants "Broadcast Audio" to the Player role (by default only trusted players have it).
Voix.MicroDonne: Players can now broadcast their microphone.

Batiments.Aide: None: a simple game, with the characters only (nothing depends on buildings, the map markers stay inert). Drawn: those of the setup. Chosen: tick those of the vigil.

Preparation.MetiersAide: Untick for a game without trades (each player has only their role).
Preparation.GazetteAide: An Event card every morning but the first (pace and choice of cards: world settings). Without the Almanac.
Preparation.CrieurAide: An office named by the Bailiff, holding Gazette cards.
Preparation.Permanentes: Permanent cards laid down from the start:

Recit.Resume: {n} (villager|villagers), {tours} round(s) in the mist. The cards turn over:
Recit.Exile: exiled by the village on turn {tour}

Chroniques.Intro: Vigils told here: {n}. AI players are not ranked.
Chroniques.Vide: No player has finished a vigil yet.
Chroniques.Lien: Every vigil and the hall of fame: {lien}.

Peste.PartieAide: No wolf: the plague strikes every night, chosen first by the narrator, then by its latest victim. Secret: the players know nothing of it.
Peste.PreparationAide: A game without any wolf: every night, the plague takes someone. The players don't know: they must find out and cry "It's the black plague!". Unchecked, a self-composed game rarely becomes one anyway.
Peste.CrierAide: If you are sure there are no wolves but a plague: the game ends and the village wins. If you are wrong, you are hanged for spreading panic.
Peste.Confirmer: Cry "It's the black plague!"? If true, the village wins. If false, you will be hanged for spreading panic.
Peste.ConfirmerPour: {nom} cries "It's the black plague!"? If false, {nom} will be hanged for spreading panic.
Peste.CriJuste: {nom} cries: "It's the black plague!" The village falls silent, then understands: there were never any wolves in Brumecombe, only the fever passing from death to death. Sheets are burned, wells are shut, and the plague retreats.
Peste.CriFaux: {nom} cries: "It's the black plague!" But the dead bear marks no fever leaves. For spreading panic, the village hangs {nom} on the spot.
Peste.InvitePorteur: The fever took you, but it is not done: in secret, choose whom it will strike tonight.
Peste.InviteNarrateur: The plague: whom does it strike tonight?
Peste.CarnetPorteur: No wolf took you: it was the black plague. There is no wolf in Brumecombe. From next night on, you will secretly choose its next victim. The living must know nothing of it.
Peste.Porteur: Plague: {nom} died of it; they will choose the next victim.
Peste.Recit: There were no wolves: the black plague prowled Brumecombe.

Refus.absent: This villager is not part of the vigil.
Refus.phase: One only cries out in broad daylight (dawn, debate, vote).
Refus.silence: Silenced, you cannot cry out today.

Bailli.Aide: The Bailiff, elected by the village: their vote counts double in the execution vote; on a tie, they decide; upon death, they name their successor.
Bailli.TuEs: You are the Bailiff: your vote counts double
Bailli.Sceau: The seal waits: {nom} names a successor
Bailli.InviteSuccession: You are dead, Bailiff. To whom do you hand the village seal?
Bailli.InviteDepartage: The vote is tied. Bailiff, decide: whom does the village condemn? ({n} at most; pass: nobody)
Bailli.Succession: {de}, the late Bailiff, hands the village seal to {nom}.
Bailli.Vacance: {de} takes the seal to the grave: the office of Bailiff stays vacant, the village will elect a new one.
Bailli.EluSort: A tie: fate names {nom}, who becomes Bailiff of Brumecombe.
Bailli.Personne: Nobody is elected: the office of Bailiff stays vacant today.
Bailli.Departage: A tie between {noms}: the Bailiff, {nom}, decides.
Bailli.TrancheVoix: A tie: the Bailiff, {nom}, had voted for {noms}; that vote breaks the tie.
Bailli.TranchePersonne: The Bailiff, {nom}, did not decide: nobody is condemned.
Bailli.Nomme: The narrator hands the village seal to {nom}, the new Bailiff.

Refus.inactif: The Bailiff is not in play in this game.
Refus.phase: The Bailiff is elected during the day.
Refus.bailli: The village already has a Bailiff.
Refus.succession: The late Bailiff has not handed over the seal yet.
Refus.deja: The village already voted for its Bailiff today.
Refus.execution: Today's execution vote has already taken place.
Refus.nomme: {nom} cannot become Bailiff (the Bailiff must be in play and the villager alive).
Refus.departage: The Bailiff must first break the tie (the narrator can decide in their place, from the Game Table).
Refus.pasDeDepartage: No tie is waiting for the Bailiff.
Refus.jourDeux: The Tenant Farmers only choose the Bailiff from the second day on.
Refus.metayers: No living Tenant Farmer can choose the Bailiff.

Bailli.SceauAttend: The seal waits: {nom}, the late Bailiff, names a successor; the count follows.
Bailli.InviteNommer: To whom does the narrator hand the village seal?
Bailli.TuEsSceau: You are the Bailiff (cracked seal: your vote is single today)

Registre.Vide: The clerk has written nothing yet.
Registre.DeclarerAide: Have a statement written in the Register, readable by the whole village (what you claim to be, what you saw). The clerk checks nothing.
Registre.Exemple: I claim to be the Ash Reader, I read…
Registre.Annonce: In the clerk's register, {nom} has this written: “{texte}”
Registre.Annule: (vote cancelled by the Justice of the Peace)

Bailli.sort: Round {tour} — {nom} becomes Bailiff, named by fate.
Bailli.succession: Round {tour} — {de}, the late Bailiff, hands the seal to {nom}.
Bailli.vacance: Round {tour} — the office of Bailiff is vacant.
Bailli.abolie: Round {tour} — {de}, pardoned, loses the office of Bailiff: Brumecombe will have no Bailiff any more.
Bailli.metayers: Round {tour} — {de}, the last Tenant Farmer, is dead: Brumecombe will have no Bailiff anymore.
Bailli.destitue: Round {tour} — Bailiff {de} is removed from office (Saint Vincent's Day).

Refus.absent: Only a villager can write in the Register.
Refus.fin: The game is over: the Register is closed.
Refus.mort: The dead no longer write in the Register.
Refus.phase: The Register is only open during the day.
Refus.silence: Silenced, you cannot declare anything during the debate or the vote.
Refus.trop: You have already had {n} statements written today.
Refus.brouillard: Thick fog: the clerk takes no statement today.

Passage.exil: Turn {tour} — {nom} is exiled by the village.

Registre.Deuil: Turn {tour} — the mourning bell tolls for time {n}.
Registre.Banc: Trial of {nom}: {pour} votes for out of {total}.

Fete.neige: Round {tour} — snow fell: the tracks are gone.
Fete.defile: Round {tour} — at the Carnival parade, the mask of {role}, which nobody wears.

Registre.Vacance: Turn {tour} — {nom} has died: their buildings stand vacant ({batiments}).

Pacte.grace: Round {tour} — {nom}, the Village Innocent, is pardoned: he will no longer vote.
Pacte.sagesse: Round {tour} — {nom}, the Greybeard, fell at the village's hand: the villagers have lost their powers.
Pacte.votants: Round {tour} — {nom}, fallen for the tie, chooses tomorrow's voters: {noms}.
Pacte.plume: Round {tour} — a black feather points at {nom}.
Pacte.second-vote: Round {tour} — a second execution vote, without debate.
Pacte.devouement: Round {tour} — {nom} steps forward: the Chambermaid takes {noms}'s card without showing it.

Village.distribution: Round {tour} — the village buildings go to {noms}; the others are Drifters.
Village.incendie: Round {tour} — {batiment} burned down; {nom} becomes a Drifter.
Village.prieur: Round {tour} — {nom}, the Prior, sees {noms}'s card in secret.
Village.remegeux: Round {tour} — {nom}, the Bonesetter, gives {noms} their power back.
Village.regent: Round {tour} — {nom}, the Schoolmaster, bars {noms} from voting.
Village.cabaret: Round {tour} — {nom}, the Alehouse Keeper, loses his immunity.

Variante.distribution: Turn {tour}: the variants of the vigil are announced.
Variante.chandelles: Night {tour}: the candles of {noms} went out together; the pack had no victim.
Variante.envoutement: Day {tour}: {nom}, condemned, was enthralled; {noms} fall along.
Variante.bailli: Day {tour}: the Bailiff {nom} votes first, openly ({noms}).

Gazette.carte: Round {tour} — {nom} reads out a Gazette card: {carte}.
Gazette.revenante: Round {tour} — {nom} comes back among the living, as a mere Villager.
Gazette.marche: Round {tour} — {nom} strikes a deal with the Devil.
Gazette.prive: Round {tour} — {nom} loses their vote for the day.
Gazette.reponse: Round {tour} — séance ({carte}): {nom} questions the spirit, who answers {reponse}.

Masques.Intro: The pack has its masks: none of these Village roles is in play. You may claim to be one of them; nobody can claim the same.
Masques.Conseil: Agree among yourselves before using them: two wolves claiming the same mask give themselves away.
Masques.Journal: Vigil masks handed to the pack: {roles}.

Souffle.Bandeau: You are dead: your last breath remains
Souffle.Voter: Last breath: your vote counts, once only

givre.Effet: Next night, no protection holds: no guard, no keeper, no lock.

crue.Effet: Next night, the Bridge is cut: the pack cannot hunt the far bank.

foire.Effet: Today, votes are cast by show of hands: everyone sees them during the vote.

brouillard.Effet: Today, the clerk sees nothing: no statement in the Register.

glas.Effet: Today, the vote names two condemned.

lune-rousse.Effet: Today, condemning needs an absolute majority.

rumeur.Effet: A true but vague rumour runs about last night.

vent-du-nord.Effet: The wind carries silences away: everyone may speak today.

sceau-brise.Effet: Today, the Bailiff's vote does not count double.

Somnambule.Devoile: {nom} was a Sleepwalker: their role was only a dream.

Calendrier.GlasAnnonce: The final knell will toll on the evening of day {n}: if the pack still lives, it will win.
Calendrier.GlasLeve: The final knell will not toll.
Calendrier.GlasAide: On the evening of that day (after its vote), the game stops: the pack wins if a wolf still lives, otherwise a living lone killer, otherwise the village.
Calendrier.Etoile: Lucky star: {nom} is secretly protected on the first night.
Calendrier.EtoileAide: The narrator secretly protects a beginner on the first night. Nobody is told.

Refus.etoile: The Lucky star only watches over the first night, before its dawn.

Passage.Aide: A traveller: everyone knows their role, nobody knows their side.
Passage.AnnonceChat: A traveller knocks at the vigil's door: {nom}, {role}, passing through Brumecombe. Nobody knows where their heart leans.
Passage.NouveauLoup: {nom}, the traveller, is one of yours: the pack has one more member.
Passage.Depart: {nom} leaves the vigil and takes to the road again.
Passage.Exil: The village drives {nom} away: the traveller takes to the road, secret and all.
Passage.QuitterAide: Must you go? You leave the game without dying: your role and side stay hidden, the game goes on without you.
Passage.QuitterQuestion: Leave the vigil? You will not be able to play this game any more.
Passage.FaireQuitterQuestion: {nom} leaves the vigil (without dying, role and side kept hidden)?
Passage.InviteAccueil: Who arrives in Brumecombe? (a connected player without a villager in play)
Passage.VoteExil: The village deliberates: should a traveller be driven away?
Passage.QuestionExil: Which traveller does the village drive away?
Passage.InviteExil: Exile vote: which traveller to drive away from the village (or nobody)?

Refus.inactif: Travellers are not admitted in this game.
Refus.phase: A traveller only arrives at dawn or during the debate.
Refus.vote: Wait for the end of the vote to welcome a traveller.
Refus.joueur: Nobody to welcome: a connected player without a villager in play is needed.
Refus.contenu: No traveller role in the content.
Refus.absent: {nom} is no longer at the vigil.

Passage.VoteSansObjet: {nom} has left the vigil: the vote is moot, nobody is designated.

Banc.AccuserAide: One accusation a day; each villager can only be accused once a day. The accused are judged one by one.
Banc.Question: Should {nom} be condemned? (voting for the accused condemns; abstaining acquits)
Banc.Invite: Trial of {nom}: vote for the accused to condemn, choose nobody to acquit.

Refus.inactif: The Dock is not in play.
Refus.phase: Accusations are only made during the debate.
Refus.absent: You have no villager in this game.
Refus.accuse: This villager is already accused today.
Refus.personne: Nobody to judge: no accused waiting (or an execution already took place today).

Deguise.MasqueTombe: {nom} was the most designated in a vote without being executed: their mask falls, visions now tell the truth about them.
Deguise.Carnet: Designated by the village without being executed, you have lost your mask: from now on, visions tell the truth about you.

Deuil.Aide: The Mourning Bell: each innocent executed tolls it, and the pack draws a power from it.
Deuil.Sonne: The mourning bell tolls over Brumecombe for time {n}.
Deuil.Pouvoir1: The bell has tolled: next night, the pack may name a villager; each wolf will learn their side.
Deuil.Pouvoir2: The bell has tolled a second time: at each execution vote, a faceless vote will join the candidate that you, the living wolves, named most.
Deuil.Pouvoir3: The bell has tolled a third time: next night, no protection will hold against the pack.
Deuil.Invite: The bell lends you its eyes: which villager do you want to see through?
Deuil.InviteVoix: The bell lends you its voice: which candidate of this vote will the faceless vote join?
Deuil.VoixChoisie: The pack places the faceless vote on {nom}.

Tablee.AnnonceTete: Small table: {humains} player(s) and {compagnons} AI companion(s). The pack is short.
Tablee.RegleLoups: The human players are never all wolves.
Tablee.RegleCamps: With three humans or more, they are never all in the same camp.
Tablee.RegleTirage: The deal favours, without guaranteeing it, a Village lantern in a human's hands.
Tablee.RegleTirageOmbre: The deal favours, without guaranteeing it, a Village lantern in a human's hands and the shadow (wolves and loners) on both sides of the table.
Tablee.RegleRythme: Ties at the vote are settled by lot, and the final bell will toll at the end of day {n}.
Tablee.NuitBlanche: Two wolves or more: the first night is a white night (the pack meets, but does not hunt), and the pack must outnumber the others to win.
Tablee.Sort: Tie: the lot settles it and names {noms}.
Tablee.PreparationAide: Small table: 1 to 4 humans, 2 to 8 AI players, 4 to 12 seats. Guaranteed: humans are never all wolves (nor all in the same camp with three or more); favoured without guarantee: a lantern with a human, the shadow on both sides of the table. Ties settled by lot; final bell at the end of day {n} (0 = automatic).

Avis.places: A small table has 4 to 12 seats: beyond that, the setup falls back to the classic level, without the mode.
Avis.humains: A small table is meant for 1 to 4 humans; beyond that, prefer a classic level.
Avis.compagnons: A small table is meant for 2 to 8 AI players: add some (« + AI player » button).

SaintMartin.Aide: One night, one vote, then the end. Three roles sleep under the Chapel altar: nobody knows which.
SaintMartin.Annonce: It is Saint Martin's night: one night, one vote. {n} roles sleep under the Chapel altar, and nobody knows which.
SaintMartin.PreparationAide: The short format (about ten minutes): one night, one vote, the end; three more roles than players, hidden under the altar.

Fetes.PreparationAide: A seasonal variant chosen for this game: the calendar holiday suggests it (pre-selected), the narrator decides. Never in a Saint Martin's Night.
Fetes.Neige: Snow this morning: the tracks are gone

Journal.Masque: Holiday vigil (secret): the Carnival mask is worn by {nom}.
Journal.Present: Holiday vigil (secret): the gift of the Lady of Bells goes to {nom}.
Journal.Promis: Holiday vigil (secret): {a} and {b} are betrothed; the pack knows.

Recit.Masque: The Carnival mask was worn by {nom}.
Recit.Present: The gift of the Lady of Bells was for {nom}; it never opened.
Recit.PresentOuvert: The gift of the Lady of Bells was for {nom}; it saved their life.

Ames.MurmureMeme: The soul of {ame} sat at the foot of your bed. It whispers that {a} and {b} are on the same side.
Ames.MurmureAutre: The soul of {ame} sat at the foot of your bed. It whispers that {a} and {b} are not on the same side.
Ames.Porte: Tonight, a soul knocked at the door of {nom}.
Ames.MjMeme: Night of Souls: the soul of {ame} whispered to {nom} that {a} and {b} are on the same side.
Ames.MjAutre: Night of Souls: the soul of {ame} whispered to {nom} that {a} and {b} are not on the same side.

nuit-des-ames.Aide: After each deadly night, the soul of the first dead whispers to a random living player whether two other living players are on the same side. But the pack hears at which door the soul knocked.
nuit-des-ames.Annonce: It is the Night of Souls: after each deadly night, the soul of the first dead will whisper a secret to someone alive… and the wolves will hear at which door it knocks.

veillee-d-hiver.Aide: A random player secretly received a gift: the first blow that should kill them at night fails. At each dawn, snow may fall (one chance in three, never two dawns in a row): that day it covers the tracks (Huntress, Chimney Sweep, Tanner, News Peddler and Wash-house learn nothing).
veillee-d-hiver.Annonce: It is the Winter Vigil: the Lady of Bells left a gift on a doorstep of Brumecombe. Once, it will save someone from a deadly blow. And when snow falls, it erases the tracks.
veillee-d-hiver.Carnet: The Lady of Bells left a gift on your doorstep: the first time a deadly blow aims at you at night, it will fail. Only once. It is up to you whether to say so.
veillee-d-hiver.Neige: Snow fell on Brumecombe tonight: it covered every track.

carnaval-des-masques.Aide: A random player secretly wears the Carnival mask: the first Village vision that falls on them sees them on the opposite side, then the mask falls; the pack's eyes are never fooled. The parade showed a mask nobody in the village wears: whoever claims it lies.
carnaval-des-masques.Annonce: It is the Carnival of Masks: someone among you wears a mask that fools visions, and only they know it.
carnaval-des-masques.Carnet: At the Carnival, the mask settled on your face: the first Village vision that falls on you (ashes, dowser, prayer) will see you on the « {camp} » side, then the mask will silently fall. The pack is never fooled. Only you know it.
carnaval-des-masques.Defile: At the Carnival parade, the mask of {role} went by: nobody in the village wears it.

fete-des-promis.Aide: Two random Village players are betrothed: each knows the other's name, a sure ally. But the betrothed show off: the pack knows both names.
fete-des-promis.Annonce: It is the Feast of the Betrothed: two Village hearts found each other in secret. The pack saw them kiss.
fete-des-promis.Carnet: For the Feast of the Betrothed, your heart is bound to {nom}'s: you were both of the Village when the roles were dealt. Only you know it… and the pack, who saw you.
fete-des-promis.Meute: The betrothed of the feast show off shamelessly: {a} and {b}, both of the Village.
fete-des-promis.AnnonceSans: It is the Feast of the Betrothed, but this year no Village hearts found each other: nobody is betrothed.

emporter.Invite: You fall, but your snares still hold: secretly choose the living villager you take into the grave (or pass).
emporter.Choisi: Last act: {nom} takes {cibles} into the grave.
emporter.Personne: {nom} chose no one (or could not answer in time): it is up to you to decide who is taken, or to say “No one”.

votants.Invite: The tie cost you your life: secretly choose who will vote tomorrow (at least one). The others will stay silent at the vote.
votants.Choisi: Last act: {nom} chooses who will vote tomorrow: {cibles}.
votants.Personne: {nom} chose no one (or could not answer in time): the whole village will vote tomorrow, unless you dictate the list (designerVotants).

Public.Annonce: {nom} holds a role known to all: {role}.

Refus.mort: {nom} is dead and can no longer hold a building.
Refus.village: This building is not part of the current “The Village” variant.
Refus.detruit: This building burned down: it no longer exists.

Pacte.Grace: {nom} is the Village Innocent: the village pardons him. He stays among you, but will never vote again.
Pacte.BailliAboli: {nom} was Bailiff: pardoned, he loses the office, and no one will take it up. Brumecombe will have no Bailiff any more.
Pacte.Sagesse: {nom}, the Greybeard, fell at the village's hand: Brumecombe has lost its wisdom. Until the end of the evening, no villager has any power left, neither from their role nor from their trade.
Pacte.Egalite: Tie: {nom} is the one who pays for those tied.
Pacte.Votants: {nom}, fallen for the tie, has chosen who will vote tomorrow: {noms}. The others will stay silent at the vote.
Pacte.PlumeMatin: A black feather points at {nom}: at today's execution vote, two more votes against them.
Pacte.PlumeVoix: The black feather weighs two votes against {nom}.
Pacte.SecondVote: A second execution vote opens at once, without debate.
Pacte.GreffierNote: {nom}, the Stammering Clerk, gave his sign: a second vote will follow the execution.
Pacte.FratrieReconnue: Tonight you open your eyes at the same time as your own: {noms}. Same blood, same side; no one else knows.
Pacte.FratrieRetrouvee: You meet in silence with {noms}: while you are awake, you may speak among yourselves.
Pacte.FratrieSeule: You wake alone: your own are gone.
Pacte.PriveDeVote: You do not vote in this vote.

Ambigus.RejointLaMeute: Tonight {nom} joins the pack: they will hunt with you.
Ambigus.ChapardeurInvite: Two cards lie face down in the middle of the table. Take one instead of yours, or pass to keep your card.
Ambigus.ChapardeurOblige: Both cards in the middle belong to the pack: you must take one.
Ambigus.ChapardeurPris: You slipped your card into the middle and took this one: you are now “{role}”, until the end of the evening.
Ambigus.ChapardeurGarde: You looked at the cards in the middle and kept your own.
Ambigus.ChapardeurNote: {nom}, the Pilferer, took the card “{role}” from the middle.
Ambigus.BateleurJoue: Tonight you play the card “{role}”: the narrator will call you in its turn. In the morning, it will be removed.
Ambigus.BateleurNote: {nom}, the Mountebank, plays the card “{role}” tonight.
Ambigus.CarteRetiree: The card “{role}” was used tonight: it is removed from the middle of the table.
Ambigus.CartesDuBateleur: Three cards are laid face up in the middle of the table: {roles}. Some night, someone may play one of them.
Ambigus.MatinMeute: You chose the pack: you hunt with it from tonight. The wolves: {noms}.
Ambigus.MatinVillage: You chose the village: you will remain a plain villager until the end.
Ambigus.MatinVillageNote: {nom}, the Mastiff, stays with the village.
Ambigus.Modele: Your model is {nom}. As long as they live, you belong to the Village; if they fall, you will join the pack.
Ambigus.ModeleNote: {nom}, the Woods Child, took {modele} as a model.
Ambigus.Orphelin: {nom}, your model, has fallen: you secretly join the pack, and will hunt with it from next night. The wolves: {noms}.
Ambigus.OrphelinNote: {modele} has fallen: {nom}, the Woods Child, joins the pack.
Ambigus.Charme: You played your hurdy-gurdy under the windows of {noms}: they are charmed.
Ambigus.Charmes: A hurdy-gurdy tune has charmed you. You open your eyes with the other charmed: {noms}. Say nothing.

Ambigus.CommenceParLeJour: This evening begins with a day: the village gathers, debates and votes before the first night.

Critere.age: by age (the young and the old)

Ambigus.ChambriereInvite: The village has condemned {noms}. Before the card is turned over, will you sacrifice yourself? Choose them to take their card (and your secret will be revealed), or pass.
Ambigus.Devouement: Before {de}'s card is turned over, {nom} reveals herself: she was the Chambermaid. She takes the condemned's card without showing it, and will hold that role until the end.
Ambigus.BailliPerdu: {nom} was Bailiff: by stepping forward, she loses the office. The village will elect another Bailiff.

Refus.tard: The Mountebank's cards are chosen before the first night.
Refus.cartes: Choose one to {n} cards of roles with a night power (neither wolf nor loner) that are not in the deck.

metayer.Aide: Tenant Farmer: from the second day on, the living Tenant Farmers choose the Bailiff among themselves; a dead Bailiff picks his successor among them. When the last Tenant Farmer dies, Brumecombe has no Bailiff anymore.

prieur.Aide: Prior: once, during the day (even after the condemned has been named), he calls a player to the priory, who shows him their card in secret.

remegeux.Aide: Bonesetter: once, during the day, he gives a player back the one-time power of their building, already spent.

regent.Aide: Schoolmaster: each day, just before the vote, he bars up to two players from voting (never a Drifter). He himself never votes.

fourniere.Aide: Oven-Keeper: each night, as the pack goes back to bed, she has a chance to glimpse one of the wolves.

perruquier.Aide: Wigmaker: once, during the day, he opens his razor on a player (never a Drifter). A wolf: the village congratulates him; otherwise he pays for his mistake with his life.

cabaretier.Aide: Alehouse Keeper: the pack cannot devour him, the village cannot vote against him; he votes in the open. If he votes against a player the vote names, he loses this immunity.

prevot.Aide: Provost: when a building is freed, he may lodge the Drifter of his choice there, who gains its power.

hobereau.Aide: Squire: once, someone condemned by the vote may beg him for mercy; he pardons them (himself too): no execution, and the card stays hidden.

chemineau.Aide: Drifter: no roof and no building power. The Schoolmaster, the Wigmaker, the Magpie and the Firebrand have no hold on him; the Provost may lodge him.

Village.IncendieProie: The flames caught the pack at {nom}'s, who escapes unharmed: {loup} perished there.
Village.Fourniere: At first light, opening the bakehouse, you glimpse {nom} slipping home along the walls: a wolf.

Village.InviteSupplique: The village has condemned you. Do you beg {nom}, the Squire, for mercy? Choose him to plead, or pass.
Village.InviteGrace: {nom} begs you for mercy: choose them to pardon them (once per game), or pass.
Village.InviteGraceSoi: The village has condemned you: choose yourself to pardon yourself (once per game), or pass.
Village.Grace: {hobereau}, the Squire, pardons {nom}: no execution, and their card stays hidden.
Village.VoteCabaret: {nom}, the Alehouse Keeper, votes in the open against {cible}.
Village.ImmunitePerdue: {nom}, the Alehouse Keeper, voted against {cible}, whom the vote named: he loses his immunity.
Village.BailliAboli: {nom} was the last Tenant Farmer: Brumecombe will have no Bailiff anymore.
Village.PreparationAide: Personalities hold the village buildings (a public power on top of their secret role); the other players are Drifters. Proposed at the deal, can be changed before the first night.
Village.Aide: Who holds which building: public, like the “visible role” token placed in front of each player. Before the first night, the narrator can change the proposal.

Variantes.PreparationAide: The party game's variants: each one is a public rule of the vigil, announced at the deal, and kept for the next one.

Chandelles.Aide: A candle per player, blown out at their death.
Chandelles.AngoissanteAide: Each wolf blows out a candle; more than one out: no victim.
Chandelles.Ratees: This morning, the candles of {noms} went out together: the pack had no victim. They are lit again.

Chaine.Aide: The execution vote is made by the chain: each seats an innocent; the last one standing is condemned.
Chaine.Invite: Chain of Innocents: name a villager still standing whose innocence you vouch for; they sit down.
Chaine.Ouverture: Chain of Innocents: the whole village stands up. {nom}, on the left of the last eliminated, names the first innocent.
Chaine.Debout: {nom} is the only one left standing: the village condemns them.
Chaine.PasDeVote: Chain of Innocents: no vote today, the chain names the condemned.

Mur.Aide: Each night, one anonymous sentence per living player; the wall is read in the morning.
Mur.Invite: Whispering Wall: write a short sentence, without your name, or pass.
Mur.Matin: On the Whispering Wall, this morning: {textes}
Mur.Muet: The Whispering Wall stayed silent tonight.

DoubleVisage.Aide: A visible role and a secret allegiance (small twist), or two secret cards (big twist).
DoubleVisage.Visible: Two Faces: {nom} shows their visible role, {role}.
DoubleVisage.CarnetPetite: Two Faces: your allegiance card is “{allegeance}”; you are of the side {camp}. Your visible role keeps its power.
DoubleVisage.CarnetGrande: Two Faces: your two secret cards are {cartes}; you are of the side {camp}.
DoubleVisage.AllegeanceLoupAide: One more wolf allegiance card in the deck (in place of a villager one). The book's deck favours the village at large tables: advised from 16 players with the small twist (and at 13), from 12 with the big one; below that, the book's deck (the pack would win seven to nine games in ten).

Vendanges.Aide: One more wolf, and every power tipsy.
Vendanges.InviteTromperie: Grape Harvest: name one of your two lovers and another player, who will love each other too, or pass.
Vendanges.BailliDabord: Grape Harvest: {nom}, the Bailiff, votes alone and first; the others wait for that vote.
Vendanges.BailliPasse: The Bailiff {nom} voted against no one.
Vendanges.AttendreLeBailli: Grape Harvest: the Bailiff votes first; wait for that vote.
Vendanges.Amour: Grape Harvest: your love forbids you to vote against this player.
Vendanges.Bouc: {nom}, the Whipping Boy, dies in place of their neighbour {voisin}.
Vendanges.Triangle: Grape Harvest: {qui} also loves {nom}; {trompe} is betrayed.

Envoutement.Aide: The pack's victims are enthralled, in secret, instead of dying.
Envoutement.Refus: You are enthralled: your powers have left you.

Quand.jamais: never at night: your power plays by day, at your death, or on its own.
Quand.meute: every night, with the whole pack, to choose the victim together.
Quand.uneSurDeux: every other night (the second, the fourth…).
Quand.impaires: the first night, then every other night (the third, the fifth…).
Quand.tantQue: every night, as long as no wolf is dead.

Explication.Question: What they will ask you:
Explication.Usages: This power can be used {n} times in the game.
Explication.VictoireVillage: with the Village, when no wolf is left alive.
Explication.VictoireMeute: with the pack, when the wolves are as many as all the other living players.

somnambule.Effet: From now on, every morning, the narrator tells everyone which role the Ash Reader read during the night, without saying whose.

inondation.Effet: The village is under water: the women take shelter in the priory, the men in the alehouse. No vote today. Next night, the pack strikes in one of the two shelters only, and may claim two victims there. (Only if at least six are still alive.)

marche-du-malin.Effet: Today, right after the verdict, each condemned player may strike a deal: this vote does not eliminate them. If they end up on the losing side, they sit out the next game.

lune-noire.Effet: The village sulks: the debate happens without looking at one another (cameras off, or text only); whoever turns towards the others loses their vote today. Everyone faces the circle again to vote.

bal-du-samedi.Effet: The younger half of the village goes dancing: the dancers neither debate nor vote, and nobody may vote against them. Next night, a dancing wolf does not hunt, and no dancer can be devoured.

cueillette.Effet: The women go foraging for the Herbalist until evening: they neither debate nor vote, and nobody may vote against them. When they return, the Herbalist refills an empty phial.

dimanche-de-soleil.Effet: Nothing special… unless the narrator decides to apply The Thrall for this round only.

pile-ou-face.Effet: Today, right after the verdict, a coin is tossed for each condemned player: heads, they are spared; tails, they are eliminated.

saint-vincent.Effet: The village wants a real leader: the current Bailiff is removed from office, and a new Bailiff is elected today.

revenante.Effet: The pack's last victim had only fainted: they come straight back among the living, but as a mere Villager.

bonnes-manieres.Effet: No interrupting: everyone speaks in turn, under the narrator's eye; whoever breaks the rule loses their vote today.

toucher-mortel.Effet: From now on, to devour its prey the pack must also mark it: after its choice, a wolf names the prey a second time; otherwise the prey is spared.

jour-des-sots.Effet: Until morning, some swap their powers: the Herbalist and the Ash Reader, the Poacher and the Mist Child, the Bridge Warden and the Greybeard. The lovers loathe each other: each must vote against the other; if one dies before morning, the other lives on.

fin-des-vendanges.Effet: Nothing special… unless the narrator decides to apply Grape Harvest for this round only.

petit-commis.Effet: The youngest goes to fetch help from the next village: today they neither debate nor vote, and next night they cannot be devoured. Back in the morning, their vote counts triple in that day's vote.

retour-de-flamme.Effet: Next night, if the pack names a mere Villager, they do not die: they become a wolf. If it names anyone else, the prey survives and the first wolf to their left is struck down. If the pack cannot agree, nobody dies.

grande-defiance.Effet: Today's vote changes: everyone gives two votes to their two favourite friends, all at once; those who receive none are eliminated.

banquet-des-veterans.Effet: The older half of the village goes feasting until evening: the veterans neither debate nor vote, and nobody may vote against them.

depit.Effet: If the next player the village eliminates is not a wolf, the village votes again at once, without debate, to eliminate a second suspect.

executeur.Effet: The village elects an Executioner. From now on, only they learn the role of those condemned by vote, which is no longer shown to anyone; they may talk about it as they please. If they die, they name a successor.

influences.Effet: The next vote is held in turn and in the open: the last player eliminated picks the first voter, then everyone votes in turn going left, with no taking it back. Votes are counted as usual.

nuit-des-sots.Effet: Next night, the wolves become readers: each reads the role of one player. The Poacher, the Herbalist and the Ash Reader become wolves: together, they eliminate a player. In the morning, everything is back to normal.

chatiment.Effet: The last player eliminated names a player: that player is eliminated, unless at least two players vouch for them. If they are slow to do so, the accused may call for help.

battue.Effet: The men go hunting until dawn: they neither debate nor vote, and nobody may vote against them. Next night, a hunting wolf does not devour, and no hunter can be devoured.

enthousiasme.Effet: If the next player the village eliminates is a wolf, the village votes again at once, without debate, to eliminate a second suspect.

enfouissement.Effet: From now on, the role of the pack's victims is never shown again.

mechant-benet.Effet: Next night, the first player eliminated in the game names a player who is not a wolf: that player learns who the wolves are and becomes their secret ally. They stay with the Village, do not wake with the wolves, and win if the wolves win.

ni-loup-ni-moi.Effet: Out of superstition, nobody may say “wolf” or “me” today (in the chat the system notices; aloud, the narrator does): whoever says them loses their vote.

lundi-gris.Effet: Nothing special… unless the narrator decides to apply Chain of Innocents for this round only.

spectre.Effet: The pack's next prey does not die: they become a wolf and name one of the former wolves, who dies at once in their place, holding the prey's former card.

cauchemar.Effet: On waking, no debate: starting to the left of the last player eliminated, each in turn accuses a villager; the most named are eliminated. This is the day's vote.

Questions.loup-sabots: Does one of the wolves wear clogs?
Questions.loup-coiffe: Does one of the wolves wear a dark headdress?

Questions.loups-femmes: Are the living wolves all women?

Gazette.SansBailli: Brumecombe has no Bailiff in this vigil: the feast changes nobody.
Gazette.Destitue: Bailiff {nom} is removed from office: the village will elect a new Bailiff today.
Gazette.PersonneARevenir: The pack has claimed no victim: nobody comes back.
Gazette.PersonnePourChatier: Nobody has fallen yet: the card has no effect.
Gazette.SotsPouvoir: Fools' Day: until morning, you hold the power of the “{role}” card (your card remains your own).

Fiole.poison: The foraging brings back enough to refill your poison phial.

Gazette.Revenante: {nom} had only fainted: they come back among the living, as a mere Villager.

Nuit.PasTouchee: No wolf marked {nom}: the prey is spared.
Nuit.Desaccord: The pack did not agree: no victim tonight.

Invite.crue: The Flood: a second prey in the same shelter as {nom}?

Invite.sots-voyance: Fools' Night: you are a reader tonight. Whose role do you read?

Chatiment.Designe: Retribution: {qui} names {nom}. At least two players must vouch for them, or they will be eliminated.
Chatiment.Sort: Retribution: {qui} named nobody; fate names {nom}. At least two players must vouch for them, or they will be eliminated.
Chatiment.InviteAppel: Retribution: call on the village for help? (naming yourself calls)
Chatiment.Appel: {nom} calls out: who will vouch for me?
Chatiment.InviteVote: Retribution: vouch for {nom} (name them); choosing nothing means staying silent.
Chatiment.Condamne: Retribution: {n} voice(s) for {nom}, not enough; {nom} is eliminated.
Chatiment.Epargne: Retribution: {n} players vouch for {nom}, who is spared.

Suite.OuvertureCauchemar: The Nightmare: no debate; each in turn, going left, accuses a villager. The most named will be eliminated.

Suite.Fenetre: Voting in turn: it is {nom}'s turn.

Defiance.SansVoix: The Great Distrust: with no vote at all, {noms} are eliminated.
Defiance.Personne: The Great Distrust: everyone received at least one vote; nobody is eliminated.
Defiance.Fenetre: The Great Distrust: choose two friends (a second click takes one back).

Invite.garder: Do you keep {nom} as Town Crier? (naming them keeps them; anyone else replaces them)
